claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule landed approximately 40 to 50 miles off the San Diego coast.
The Artemis II Orion capsule landed at roughly 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The splashdown ended a 10-day crewed mission around the Moon.
Splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
A joint NASA and U.S. Navy team including the USS John P. Murtha recovered the astronauts and capsule.
The crew was retrieved via helicopter.
The crew was taken to the USS John P. Murtha for initial medical evaluations before returning to shore.
The splashdown concluded the first crewed lunar flyby in over 50 years.
The spacecraft was expected to enter from the southwest.
